headline: High: Claude Code can read/write the shared workspace while Authelia exposes broad network/OAuth surfaces, creating default-path data leakage and cascading-error risk.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Claude Code can read repo files and user-provided directories, and shared filesystem state is its documented bridge to other instances. Authelia exposes OAuth/ForwardAuth and broad network egress, so if its outputs are written into shared files, Claude Code may treat attacker-controlled content as instructions. No direct shared channel is documented beyond files, so I choose medium, not low.
conditions: IF Authelia writes untrusted content into a file that Claude Code later reads
IF Claude Code is pointed at the same workspace or repo files as Authelia's outputs
mitigations: Separate workspaces for the two agents
Mark Authelia-generated files as data-only and never executable
Add a manual review step before Claude Code consumes Authelia output
Use read-only mounts for Authelia output directories
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for shared files

B_data_leakage.rationale: Claude Code explicitly reads repo files and user-provided directories and handles git history and shell environment, while Authelia has broad network egress and OAuth/ForwardAuth surfaces. If sensitive files are present in the shared workspace, Claude Code can ingest them and Authelia can move related context over the network. The pair has a plausible shared-workspace leakage path in default use, so medium fits.
conditions: IF sensitive files are placed in the shared cwd or repo
IF Authelia is configured to forward or proxy those files or their metadata over the network
mitigations: Keep secrets out of the shared workspace
Use separate service accounts and directories
Restrict Authelia to non-sensitive test data
Review outbound destinations before enabling network paths
requires-engineering: enforce workspace-level DLP

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Claude Code can write the filesystem, modify git state, and spawn subprocesses; Authelia is network-facing and can call OAuth/ForwardAuth APIs. Their overlap on mutable workspace state plus git makes concurrent edits and state corruption plausible by default when both touch the same repo. The rubric’s high indicator is close enough that uncertainty should escalate upward.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same directory or git repository
IF Authelia writes artifacts that Claude Code also edits or commits
mitigations: Assign separate repos or branches
Serialize writes with a lock file
Disable git writes for one agent during the other's run
Use a staging directory for Authelia outputs
requires-engineering: add optimistic-concurrency checks

D_cascading_error.rationale: Claude Code can act on files and git state, so if it consumes Authelia-produced outputs without verification, errors can cascade into commits or shell actions. Authelia’s network/OAuth surfaces make it a plausible upstream producer of machine-readable artifacts, but there is no direct evidence of an automated handoff. That supports medium rather than high.
conditions: IF Claude Code treats Authelia output as authoritative input
IF Claude Code is allowed to commit or execute actions based on that output
mitigations: Require human review before commits
Add schema validation for Authelia outputs
Use a checksum or signature on handoff files
Limit Claude Code to dry-run mode for generated artifacts
requires-engineering: add verification gates before action-taking

E_compliance.rationale: Authelia is an authentication service with broad network/OAuth surfaces, while Claude Code handles repo files, git history, and environment secrets. The profiles do not show a residency or certification mismatch, so only a generic compliance gap is visible: if regulated data enters Claude Code’s workspace, retention and logging obligations may differ. The other agent is cited because the risk is pairwise through shared data handling.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in the shared workspace
IF Claude Code logs or retains that data longer than Authelia's policy allows
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the shared repo
Document retention expectations for both tools
Use redacted test fixtures
Review logging settings before use
requires-engineering: align retention and deletion workflows
